requirement:
The Python outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Functions and methods | `def` | Declared name |
| Classes | `class` | Declared name |

Nested definitions appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Decorators attach to the definition they decorate and are included in its
selected source and structural hash.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.python.items`.

**Kinds and names**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[python_profile_outlines_defs_classes_and_statements]` asserts `def[f]`, `class[C]` and the method `class[C]/def[m]`. It also asserts line spans and that top-level non-definition statements map to the root.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[python_nested_definitions_use_the_nearest_outline_ancestor]` asserts the full selector list. It includes `async def`, which gets kind `def` with its declared name.

**Nesting under the nearest enclosing outline item**
- The same nested test asserts class-in-class and a method in an inner class.
- It asserts a `def local` inside an `if` inside a method, which sits under `def[method]`. The non-outline `if` is skipped.
- It asserts a class and method inside a function, and an async function inside an async function.

**Decorators in selected source**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[python_selected_source_includes_its_decorators]` asserts that the selected text of a decorated function equals the whole source, decorator included, and that the item span starts at 0.
- It asserts that decorated classes select text starting with their own decorator.
- The nested test asserts that a decorated method's selected text starts with `@decorate`.

**Decorators in structural hash**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing]` asserts that changing or removing the decorator changes the function's hash. It also asserts that blank lines between the decorator and the `def` leave the hash unchanged.
- It asserts that a method's decorator edit changes the enclosing class's structural hash.

**Cited selector requirement** (`requirements.references.outline_selectors`)
- This is context only. Its duplicate-name suffix applies to this subject's case, and the decorated-class test covers it. Two classes named `Checked` select as `class[Checked]#1` and `class[Checked]#2`, each with its own decorator.
- Percent encoding and anonymous identities do not arise for Python `def` and `class` names.

I found no gap that needs a new test or marker. All four tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} items
The Python outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Functions and methods | `def` | Declared name |
| Classes | `class` | Declared name |
Nested definitions appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Decorators attach to the definition they decorate and are included in its
selected source and structural hash.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
